manager.menuHint: Open the House Rules Manager to enable or disable individual house rules for this world.
manager.reloadNotice: House rules updated. Reload Foundry so every connected client applies the change.

example.title: Example House Rule (template)
example.hint: Disabled by default. Copy the houserules/_example folder to create a new house rule; this one only logs a message to the console when enabled, as a working template.

exhaustionOnDrop.title: Exhaustion after a Knockout
exhaustionOnDrop.hint: A player character who ends up at 0 HP gains one level of exhaustion the moment they are healed back above 0 HP - not the instant they drop. No cap per rest: every time they are brought back up is another level, and a character who is never healed above 0 HP gains nothing. Only affects player characters, not NPCs/allies.

moraleCheck.title: Morale Checks
moraleCheck.hint: Adds a leader token status and a half-HP/leader-down GM reminder for morale checks, plus a rollMoraleCheck() macro API (DC 10 Wisdom save) for targeted NPCs. Fleeing/surrendering stays your call.
moraleCheck.reminderHalfHp: Morale check reminder: {name} just dropped to half HP or less.
moraleCheck.reminderLeaderDown: Morale check reminder: {name} (marked as leader) was just dropped.
moraleCheck.noTargets: No targeted or selected NPC tokens to roll a morale check for.
moraleCheck.autoFail: {name} automatically fails its morale check (overwhelming odds).

lingeringInjury.title: Lingering Injury instead of Massive Damage death
lingeringInjury.hint: When a hit's leftover damage after dropping a PC to 0 HP would equal/exceed their HP max (the DMG's Massive Damage instant-death rule, which dnd5e does not automate), this rolls a Lingering Injury instead and applies it as an Active Effect, with its mechanical penalty already automated (disadvantage, attack roll penalties, speed, max HP, ability scores). Player characters only. Remove the effect manually once resolved.
lingeringInjury.announcement: {name} takes a blow that should have been fatal - instead they're left with: {injury}.

rib.name: Cracked Rib
rib.description: Sharp pain on any strenuous physical effort.

tendon.name: Torn Tendon
tendon.description: One limb responds sluggishly; sudden, forceful movements with it are difficult.
tendon.mechanic: Speed reduced by 5 feet (1.5 m) and -1 to melee attack rolls.

eye.name: Wounded Eye
eye.description: Peripheral vision on that side is badly compromised.
eye.mechanic: Disadvantage on Perception checks and -2 to ranged attack rolls.

head.name: Head Trauma
head.mechanic: Disadvantage on concentration saves and on initiative rolls.

scar.name: Deep Scar
scar.description: A permanent mark - mostly cosmetic, but the wound underneath never quite healed right.

nerve.name: Damaged Nerve
nerve.description: That hand's grip can no longer be trusted the way it used to be.

constitution.name: Weakened Constitution
constitution.description: The body never truly recovered from that blow.

breath.name: Shortness of Breath
breath.description: Lungs struggle after any sustained exertion.
breath.mechanic: Speed reduced by 5 feet (1.5 m) and disadvantage on Constitution checks.

slowNaturalHealing.title: Slow Natural Healing
slowNaturalHealing.hint: A long rest no longer restores hit points on its own: the only way back up is spending Hit Dice (the DMG's Slow Natural Healing variant). Everything else about the rest is unchanged - Hit Dice, spell slots, item uses and the level of exhaustion it removes. Applies to every actor, NPCs included.
slowNaturalHealing.spendLabel: Spend Hit Dice once the rest is over
slowNaturalHealing.spendHint: Rolls Hit Dice until you are nearly at full HP or you run out - it will empty the reserve if that is what it takes. Dice spent now stay spent until the next long rest.
